selected_evidence.requirement: opsadmin has the requested public key
selected_evidence.summary: Verified the account, exact authorized-key match, locked password, 0700 home/.ssh permissions, 0600 authorized_keys permissions, and ED25519 fingerprint SHA256:dzumj/cx0zCYHF+qGqYpYxim69qp3tvnujZ1d97UGls.

Effective sshd configuration has public-key authentication enabled, password and keyboard-interactive authentication disabled, and AuthenticationMethods set to publickey. Live probes showed only publickey offered.

Captured healthy baseline and restart acknowledgement; boot ID changed from 7696f701-f595-4749-ab34-ce04ad7e86b7 to 59c0df36-7f2c-45b6-b9c9-f9872690d7ac. After restart, sshd was started and listening on port 22, key-only behavior remained active, and the account/key persisted.

# Managed benchmark requirement: public-key SSH authentication only.
PubkeyAuthentication yes
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
AuthenticationMethods publickey
ANTRIEB_EOF

rc-service sshd reload
printf '%s\n' 'effective:'
